 Lucasfilm Officially Confirms Several Reimaginings of ‘Star Wars: A New Hope’
 in Entertainment , Star Wars 
 Posted on November 10, 2026 by Daniel Roberts 
 Leave a comment 
 Credit: Lucasfilm
 Few movies inspire the same devotion as Star Wars (1977). George Lucas’ original film, which introduced audiences to characters such as Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), Princess Leia (Carrie Fisher), and Han Solo (Harrison Ford) , quickly became one of the biggest entertainment franchises in history, spanning toys, animation, theme parks, video games, comics, and beyond.
 Almost 50 years later, fans remain fiercely protective of the film that started it all. Even the smallest changes have sparked passionate debate.
 Credit: Lucasfilm 
 Related:  Meet the New Luke, Han, and Leia Actors in Official New ‘Star Wars’ Project 
 Star Wars: A New Hope Is Being Reimagined
 As the film approaches its 50th anniversary in 2027, the studio is preparing several official reimaginings of the original adventure, giving audiences entirely different ways to experience the story.
 First up is Star Wars: A New Hope – Triple Take , a graphic novel arriving in April 2027. Written by Kim Shearer and Chas! Pangburn, the project retells the events of the original film through the perspectives of Luke, Leia, and Han, with each character remembering the adventure differently.
 Credit: Lucasfilm 
 Then there’s Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles , a six-issue crossover written by Kevin Smith. This time, characters from the original film will encounter familiar superheroes and villains, including Spider-Man, the Avengers, and Doctor Doom. The first issue is scheduled to arrive in January 2027.
 Lucasfilm is also preparing something for Welsh-speaking audiences. Star Wars: Gobaith Newydd  is an official Welsh-language dub of the 1977 film, featuring Matthew Rhys (Han Solo), Rhys Ifans (Obi-Wan Kenobi), and Aimee-Ffion Edwards (Princess Leia). It will premiere on S4C and its streaming services on Christmas Day 2026.
 Last but not least, Star Wars: A New Hope – The Complete Manga will collect all four volumes of Hisao Tamaki’s classic manga adaptation in a deluxe omnibus, bringing the original adventure back in a distinctive Japanese comic-book style. It’s scheduled for release in March 2027.
 Whether through new perspectives, unexpected crossovers, another language, or a completely different artistic style, Lucasfilm clearly isn’t finished revisiting the story that started it all.
 Credit: Lucasfilm 
 These projects are just part of the wider 50th-anniversary celebrations.
 Star Wars: The Experience – A Journey Through the Galaxy , an exhibition featuring costumes, props, and interactive displays, will open at Philadelphia’s Franklin Institute on February 13, 2027, ahead of a five-year North American tour.
 A newly restored version of the original 1977 theatrical release will also return to theaters on February 19.
 Meanwhile, UK fans will have two ways to experience the saga with a live orchestra : Star Wars: A New Hope in Concert will tour Sheffield City Hall (March 21), Birmingham’s Symphony Hall (March 25), and Glasgow Royal Concert Hall (March 27), while London’s Royal Albert Hall will host Star Wars Weekender from April 29 to May 2, featuring screenings of all three original trilogy films accompanied by the London Symphony Orchestra.
 Which of these upcoming Star Wars projects are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments!
